title: Enterprise reservation adjudication and GPU classification procedure
creator: Asha Patel
description: Create an adjudication procedure and decision checklist for enterprise reserved capacity requests. Objective: provide a repeatable triage path that converts customer asks (SLA targets, sustained/reserved throughput, GPU family preference, burst policies, and scaling tolerance) into a single recommended reservation profile and a set of negotiation talking points. This ticket produces the checklist, classification rules for GPU families (memory bound vs compute bound workloads), scaling policy templates (static reserve, autoscale-with-burst, hybrid pre-warm), and a short decision log for stakeholders.
background: We currently intake dedicated capacity requests ad-hoc across sales and solutions engineering. That leads to inconsistent commitments (overprovisioning to avoid misses, or underprovisioning with unexpected SLA violations) and long back-and-forths during procurement. This procedure aims to shorten sales cycles and make engineering onboarding predictable while protecting platform capacity.
proposed_solution: 1) Intake form that converts customer answers into scored dimensions: latency SLO, P99 SLO, tokens/sec sustained, burst factor, KV cache reuse rate, model family (decoder-only vs mixture), regulatory isolation, and preferred GPU classes. 2) Scoring matrix maps dimensions to three reserve archetypes: Predictable (static reserve), Elastic (autoscale + burst credits), and Conservative (higher reserve + buffer). 3) GPU classification rules: allocate A100/RTX6000 for memory-bound large context inferencing; H100 for mixed memory/throughput with fp16; L4/L40 for low-latency smaller model footprints. 4) Template SLA clauses and negotiation script for Sales/CS. 5) Engineering runbook for onboarding and capacity-change requests.
acceptance_criteria: A single-page adjudication checklist that converts intake form results into a recommended reserve archetype and suggested GPU classes
Scoring matrix documented and validated against 5 historical enterprise requests (compare recommended vs actual outcome)
Scaling policy templates (static, autoscale-with-burst, hybrid) with clear rollback and fallback behaviors
At least two Sales/SE roleplay sessions documented and signed off by Solutions Eng and Platform Eng
A 1-hour onboarding runbook for infra ops with checklist and monitoring dashboard links
decision_log: 2025-02-12: Decided to favor a scored rather than purely rules-based approach to capture gray area trade-offs (e.g., high burst + low sustained implies autoscale-with-burst but may need compute-class GPUs). 2025-02-14: Agreed GPU classification should be recommendations not hard constraints; allow customers to opt for lower-cost GPU with documented tradeoffs. 2025-02-18: Chose three archetypes to keep sales conversations simple (Predictable, Elastic, Conservative). Open: how to price burst credits and how to enforce sustained throughput guarantees across multi-tenant Dedicated pools.
open_questions: What is the canonical unit for sustained throughput in customer contracts? (tokens/sec vs requests/sec vs model-specific token mix)
How do we charge for burst credits without disincentivizing customers from using useful short spikes?
Should GPU family recommendations be tied to specific model size thresholds or to customer-specified max_context and batch profiles?
